gbm_population_evidence.quote: Newly-diagnosed, histologically proven, intracranial glioblastoma with maximal safe resection.

candidate_evidence.quote: The hypothesis of this trial is that in elderly GBM patients with poor performance status (age ≥ 65 years and KPS 60-70), a chemotherapy alone (TMZ monotherapy) approach to therapy results in non-inferior overall survival compared to combined TMZ/RT.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Chemo-Radiotherapy Versus Chemotherapy for Elderly and Frail Patients With Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma

role_evidence.quote: Temozolomide (TMZ) daily for 21 days, followed by up to 6 cycles of adjuvant TMZ, as tolerated. If tolerated, additional cycles of adjuvant TMZ may be administered.
To compare overall survival of standard therapy vs chemotherapy in elderly and frail patients with newly diagnosed GBM.

arms: Standard Arm: TMZ with concurrent RT (combined modality arm)

source_quote.quote: MGMT promoter methylation status must be tested and the results positive (defined as all non-negative MGMT status, including intermediate or indeterminate status (i.e., with cutoff higher than the MGMT negative threshold).

coder_notes: Randomised TMZ alone (experimental) vs TMZ/RT (active comparator, registered as combination product) in elderly frail MGMT-methylated newly diagnosed GBM. Temozolomide is an established GBM therapy tested in a new setting (without RT), so established_therapy_experiment; it is also the backbone in the comparator arm (role there would be control/soc). Registered as one TMZ row covering both arms. No candidate agent.
